transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alice (Redwood AE), Ben (Redwood SE), Claire (Silverpine Head InfoSec), Dan (Cloud Architect), Maya (Compliance)

Summary: quick posture review focused on how Redwood surfaces SOC 2/ISO artifacts, trust center access patterns, and KMS/RBAC flows for evidence orchestration. Customer is evaluating hosted + VPC options; main blockers are log residency and proof of key custody.

Topics: Trust Center access, redacted SOC 2 artifacts, RBAC/SSO mapping, audit log export and retention, KMS integration (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), controls mapping for ISO27001 scope.

00:00 Alice (AE): All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros, I'm Alice Ramos from Redwood, AE.
00:12 Ben (SE): Ben Cho, engineering, I'll be covering the KMS and logging bits.
:18 Claire Norton: Claire Norton, Head of InfoSec at Silverpine, hi.
00:25 Dan Ortiz: Dan here, cloud architect.
00:28 Maya Singh: Maya, compliance manager. Thanks.
00:34 Alice: Quick agenda, we'll run through how you can access the Trust Center, what reports we can surface, then Ben will walk KMS and RBAC flows, then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
00:42 Claire: Yep, please — especially the trust center access and what we can download for audit.

01:02 Ben (SE): Ok jumping in: on KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS — we call it "BYOK flow"; there is an HSM-backed option with envelope encryption so the model tokens are encrypted at rest with your key.
01:24 Dan: When you say "BYOK flow" is that limited to cloud KMS providers or do you support HSM appliances on-prem?
01:34 Ben: Right now main integrations are AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, but we do have an on-prem HSM partner for Private deployments; for hosted you can bring your key via AWS/GCP/Azure APIs. Sorry, the transcript is a little rough — we have an h s m partner.
01:50 Claire: Important for us: key escrow and proof of custody — auditors want to see evidence we control the keys for certain datasets, but also the logs showing key use. Can Redwood provide that?
02:06 Ben: Yes, we produce key usage audit logs tied to request IDs. You can get a per-tenant view showing key-unwrap operations and timestamps; retention is configurable depending on your plan.
02:19 Maya: retention windows — we have to keep logs for seven years for a subset of payments evidence. Is that feasible?
02:28 Ben: Seven years on raw logs is heavy. Hosted plan retention tiers go up to 3 years by default; beyond that we'd map to long-term storage export. For Dedicated/Private we recommend streaming logs to your S3/Blob for long term retention.
02:44 Dan: So if we onboard to Dedicated, we'd be able to push audit logs to our bucket in eu-central-1 and keep for seven years?
02:53 Ben: Correct, that's standard: log forwarding to customer-owned buckets with lifecycle rules.

03:10 Alice: On the Trust Center: we can grant view-only access to your security and audit teams, or we can provide redacted SOC 2 Type II artifacts directly. Claire, which would you prefer?
03:21 Claire: Prefer direct access, but auditors want machine-readable control mapping and evidence references; we need to map our controls to Redwood controls in our ISO matrix.
03:32 Alice: Understood. We have a controls-mapping CSV that ties Redwood controls to SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 annex A. We can share that and mark which artifacts are downloadable versus available on request.
03:46 Maya: When you say downloadable artifacts — are test results and raw logs included? Or only summaries? Auditors ask for chain-of-custody.
03:55 Alice: Test reports are downloadable (redacted), but raw tenant logs are not exposed from the hosted control plane — those are always exported to you or stored in your Dedicated environment. We can, however, provide signed attestations and hashes for artifact integrity.
04:12 Claire: Ok that helps. For our internal checklist we need: SOC2 Type II, control mapping CSV, sample audit logs for key events, SSO/SAML config doc, and KMS key usage report.
04:25 Alice: We'll package that.

05:01 Dan: A question on RBAC: we run Okta for SSO, and we'll want to map Okta groups to Redwood roles with least privilege; can Redwood show the mapping and a sample SCIM sync?
05:17 Ben: Yep, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning. Roles are pluggable; we have default roles (admin, auditor, developer) and you can add custom roles with granular permissions. SCIM sync logs are available for audit.
05:34 Dan: Any known gotchas with SCIM and group nesting? We use nested groups extensively.
05:41 Ben: Nested group support is limited in a few older SCIM clients; we recommend testing via a small pilot. We'll include a SCIM caveats doc.

06:05 Claire: Can we restrict who in our org can request evidence? We need segregation: only compliance can download certain artifacts.
06:13 Alice: Yes, RBAC supports role-level restrictions for Trust Center actions. We can lock evidence exports to a "compliance" role. For hosted customers we do identity federation to Okta and map groups accordingly.

07:00 Maya: A few auditors flagged the "redacted SOC2" — they sometimes want the management answers and the control test sample. How redacted are they in practice?
07:12 Alice: We typically remove tenant-identifying info from sample test records but include the test scope, frequency, and samples. For deeper dives we can arrange a restricted auditor access workflow or an NDA and provide less redacted material.
07:26 Claire: Would the NDA flow be manual? Or is there an auditor self-serve in Trust Center?
07:32 Alice: We have two options: self-serve read-only Trust Center accounts for auditor emails you register, or a managed auditor access where we issue time-limited credentials after a signed NDA. Both have audit trails.

08:05 Ben: Shifting back to logs — we tag every request with a correlation ID and model variant id, plus a route id. For any audit you can trace from a model output back to the request + key use + deployment node.
08:20 Dan: Do you ingest those logs into a SIEM-friendly format? Splunk, Elastic?
08:27 Ben: Yes, JSON payloads with schema docs; we have exporters for Splunk, Elastic, and native S3. We can provide a sample ingestion config.

09:00 Claire: Data residency question — we process EU customer data so we need all inference logs and embeddings stored in eu-west-1. If we use hosted, can Redwood pin logs and key storage to region?
09:12 Alice: We can pin to region for most artifacts; hosted model execution may still route to nearest compute region but logs and persisted artifacts can be configured to be stored in eu-west-1. For strict residency we often recommend Dedicated or Private.
09:28 Dan: If runtime compute happens outside EU region, does that violate residency? Auditors ask about in-transit protections.
09:36 Ben: Good point — runtime in a different region can be an issue. For strict residency, Dedicated in-region is best. If you must use hosted with regional pinning, we provide full encryption in transit and at rest and export all logs to your EU bucket. We'll document the exact flow.

10:10 Maya: A smaller point — do you retain full prompt text in logs? We'll need to redact PCI or PII.
10:19 Ben: By default we keep request/response metadata; full prompt retention is configurable. We can redact or exclude prompt bodies, or obfuscate sensitive slots. There's a proxied ingestion layer where you can set tokenization/redaction rules before logs persist.

12:00 Claire: For ISO mapping, our auditor wants Annex A controls mapped to specific Redwood features — e.g., A.10 crypto controls -> KMS details, A.8 asset management -> deployment inventory. Is that CSV mapping you mentioned exhaustive?
12:18 Alice: It's fairly granular: we map control to Redwood product artifact, evidence type, and where to find it in Trust Center. We'll attach the CSV and sample ISO mapping template.

15:10 Dan: On evidence collection — if an auditor wants a play-by-play of a single production incident with raw logs, what's the mechanism?
15:21 Ben: You can open a trust request ticket; in Dedicated we can hand over a tarball of logs for a timeframe with signed hashes. For hosted, it's similar but logs must first be exported to your bucket; we provide the signed artifact and chain-of-custody.

18:00 Claire: Are there SLA clauses around evidence delivery times? Auditors often ask for turn-around times.
18:10 Alice: For enterprise contracts we define evidence delivery SLAs—typically 3–5 business days for a standard artifact package. Emergency pulls can be faster under a higher support tier.

21:00 Maya: Encryption at rest — aside from KMS, do you use envelope encryption and per-tenant keys?
21:10 Ben: Envelope encryption yes; per-tenant keys is supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be per-customer key if you bring your key.

24:00 Dan: A technical note — how are KV caches handled in dumps? Our legal team is concerned about cached prefixes being stored.
24:12 Ben: KV cache contents are ephemeral in memory for runtime performance; we don't persist full KV cache to long-term storage. Checkpoints are logged as metadata only. I'll be explicit in the doc: KV cache not persisted unless you snapshot intentionally.

28:00 Claire: Could you show a short demo of the Trust Center? Even a walkthrough would help us see where mapping lives.
28:09 Alice: Sure — we'll follow up with a recorded walkthrough in the next email. In this call I'll narrate: top-level shows compliance reports, below that control mapping, artifacts pane includes downloadable redacted reports and request evidence button.
28:30 Dan: And the request evidence button creates an audit trail?
28:34 Alice: Yes it records requester, timestamp, reason, and any attached NDA reference.

32:00 Maya: A risk item — our board wants assurance around third-party subprocessors. How does Redwood publish changes?
32:10 Alice: We have a subprocessors list in Trust Center and notify customers on changes with 30-day notice for major ones. There's also a data flow diagram and subprocessors page.

36:00 Claire: For ISO, we'll need statements of applicability and control owners. Can Redwood provide named control owners for platform controls?
36:11 Alice: We can provide the control owner job function (e.g., "Platform Security Team") and a contact alias for audit purposes. Named individuals rarely included in standard artifacts but we can coordinate for NDAed auditor access.

40:00 Dan: One last technical wrinkle — network logs for egress to model serving nodes, are those included in the audit bundle?
40:10 Ben: Yes, network flow logs can be included when exporting incident bundles; they will be part of the tarball along with timestamps and correlation ids.

44:00 Claire: Ok, decision criteria — our internal checklist: 1) Trust Center access for audit team, 2) KMS key custody proof, 3) evidence export SLA, 4) region pinning for logs or Dedicated option. If Redwood can meet those, we move to POC.
44:23 Alice: That's helpful — summary then: we'll send redacted SOC2 report, controls mapping CSV, sample KMS usage log, SCIM caveats doc, and recorded Trust Center walkthrough. We'll also draft a POC runbook for evidence export to your EU bucket.

44:40 Dan: Typo? (laughs)
44:42 Alice: Sorry left a stray slash.

48:00 Maya: Timeline — we'd like the POC the week of 2026-05-18 and procurement decisions by end of June. Is that realistic?
48:10 Alice: Yes that aligns with typical timelines; we'll aim to have artifacts by 2026-05-06 and the POC scheduled the week of 5/18.

51:00 Claire: Any blockers from Redwood side?
51:06 Ben: No blockers; we'll need a list of auditor emails if you want self-serve access, and your S3 bucket info for log export for the POC.
51:20 Alice: Great—I'll follow up with the email that has the Trust Center link and the SOC2 redaction guidance.
51:30 Claire: Thanks everyone.
51:35 Dan: Thanks.
51:40 Maya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
